- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from sentiment pivot point.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30d average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30d horizon, model underestimates early in the period when sentiment is weak; add 0.5–1.0% to first 5–7 days if sentiment <0.5.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment; if sentiment >0.7 and price <prev, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day.
